nodes.label: Narrative Flattening in LLM Fiction
nodes.author: Zehan Li, Yutong Zhu, Siyang Wu, Honglin Bao, James A. Evans
nodes.rationale: Empirical study measuring how post-training (SFT, DPO, RLVR) compresses narrative variation in LLM-generated fiction across three dimensions: thematic motion, affective prevalence, and linguistic diversity. Demonstrates that alignment produces domain-insensitive convergence toward a narrow continuation regime, with largest compression for professional literary fiction.

nodes.label: Narrative Flattening: Post-Training Compression of Story Variation
nodes.rationale: Measurable compression of narrative variation across three dimensions: (1) thematic motion becomes more uniform (topic-jump CV drops 22.2% from human baseline), (2) high-arousal emotions (conflict, surprise-curiosity) are suppressed while neutral affect rises, (3) linguistic diversity collapses with cross-domain style divergence dropping 90%. Post-training installs a fixed writing regime insensitive to source domain complexity.

nodes.label: Alignment-Induced Homogenization in Open-Ended Generation
nodes.rationale: Post-training through SFT, DPO, and RLVR reduces output diversity and narrows distributions. Base model shows stylistic sprawl (6× human variance); SFT collapses to 0.84×; DPO/RLVR to 0.5–0.55×. Professional literary fiction compressed most (21pp affective drop) because its baseline lies farthest from aligned model's attractor; common fiction shows smaller gaps because baselines already sit closer to convergence point.

nodes.label: Domain-Insensitive Convergence Under Post-Training
nodes.rationale: Post-trained endpoints converge across domains: cross-domain thematic CV spread shrinks 62%, affective charge spread 81%, style MMD² drops from 0.61 to ~0.01. Model applies single continuation regime regardless of source domain, erasing distinctions between professional literary fiction, prompt-guided stories, and public-platform fiction. Convergence point sits closer to common-fiction baselines than literary fiction.

nodes.label: Post-Training as Narrative Regularization
nodes.rationale: Post-training acts as regularization of narrative trajectory, not parametric optimization. Base model is affectively over-marked and stylistically unstable. SFT, DPO, RLVR make generation more controlled and conventionally well-formed by suppressing variation: thematic jumps become uniform, affect muted, linguistic habits collapse. Control achieved through loss of dynamic contrast—possible structural account of why aligned fiction feels mechanical.

nodes.label: Distinct Alignment Objectives Needed for Creative Writing
nodes.rationale: Creative-writing assistants require alignment objectives distinct from general-purpose assistants. In summarization, reduced variation is desirable; in fiction, variation leads to heightened experience. Possible directions: domain-conditional reward models calibrating to source register; distributional matching objectives preserving variation within and across stories; preference data deliberately sampled from literary tail rather than majority-preferred continuations.

nodes.label: Narrative Flattening in LLM Story Continuation
nodes.rationale: Core research paper analyzing how post-training (SFT, DPO, RLVR) compresses narrative diversity in LLM-generated story continuations across thematic, affective, and stylistic dimensions.

nodes.label: The New Yorker Short Fiction Corpus (1945-2019)
nodes.rationale: Restricted corpus of 3,023 professional literary short stories under 5,000 words used as primary evaluation domain for narrative analysis.

nodes.label: TELL ME A STORY (TMAS) Corpus
nodes.rationale: Publicly available corpus of 230 human-written stories composed in guided creative-writing setting, providing prompt-guided fiction baseline.

nodes.label: StoryStar Public Platform Fiction Corpus
nodes.rationale: 100 short stories from storystar.com public creative-writing platform, representing minimal editorial filtering baseline.

nodes.label: OLMo 32B Base
nodes.rationale: Base checkpoint (allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B) used as starting point for instruction-tuning pipeline in stage-wise analysis.

nodes.label: OLMo 32B SFT
nodes.rationale: Supervised fine-tuning checkpoint (allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct-SFT) representing first post-training stage.

nodes.label: OLMo 32B DPO
nodes.rationale: Direct Preference Optimization checkpoint (allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct-DPO) representing second post-training stage.

nodes.label: OLMo 32B RLVR
nodes.rationale: Final instruction-tuned checkpoint (allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct) representing full post-training pipeline endpoint.

nodes.label: Thematic Motion Coefficient of Variation
nodes.rationale: Measures narrative rhythm by computing coefficient of variation of adjacent-sentence semantic distances using text-embedding-3-large; lower CV indicates flatter, more regularized narrative structure.

nodes.label: Affective Charge Prevalence
nodes.rationale: Aggregates surprise-curiosity and conflict affect families from GoEmotions-adapted classifier; measures emotional intensity in narrative.

nodes.label: Style Maximum Mean Discrepancy
nodes.rationale: Measures linguistic-habit distance between human and model style distributions using StyleDistance embeddings with Gaussian RBF kernel; lower MMD indicates closer style alignment.

nodes.label: Literary-Adapted GoEmotions Classifier
nodes.rationale: Fine-tuned RoBERTa-based affect classifier adapted from GoEmotions to literary prose using 12,000-sentence adaptation set with LLM distillation and human validation (κ=0.68).

nodes.label: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large
nodes.rationale: 3072-dimensional embedding model used for thematic motion analysis; provides semantic representation of story sentences for computing adjacent-sentence distances.

nodes.label: StyleDistance Embeddings
nodes.rationale: 768-dimensional SentenceTransformer-based embeddings trained on human-authored text for content-independent style analysis; used for MMD and across-story variance computations.

nodes.label: Thematic Rhythm Compression Across Post-Training
nodes.rationale: Post-training stages (SFT, DPO, RLVR) progressively reduce thematic CV from 0.104 (human) to 0.081 (RLVR) on New Yorker; effect is monotonic and saturates at DPO/RLVR.

nodes.label: Affective Neutralization in Aligned Models
nodes.rationale: Instruction-tuning sharply reduces affective charge (41.0% → 20.7% on New Yorker) while raising neutral narration (28.7% → 45.1%); effect is most consistent across model families.

nodes.label: Across-Story Style Variance Collapse
nodes.rationale: Post-training reduces across-story style variance to 0.29-0.37× human levels; effect is largest in professional fiction (New Yorker) and domain-dependent across model families.

nodes.label: Register, Genre, and Style (Biber & Conrad 2009)
nodes.author: Douglas Biber, Susan Conrad
nodes.rationale: Foundational work on linguistic register and style variation; cited for theoretical grounding of stylistic analysis in narrative.

nodes.label: Stories are to entertain: A structural-affect theory (Brewer & Lichtenstein 1982)
nodes.author: William F. Brewer, Edward H. Lichtenstein
nodes.rationale: Theoretical framework linking narrative structure to affective response; motivates affective analysis of story continuations.

nodes.label: GoEmotions: A dataset of fine-grained emotions (Demszky et al. 2020)
nodes.author: Dorottya Demszky, Dana Movshovitz-Attias, Jeongwoo Ko, Alan Cowen, Gaurav Nemade, Sujith Ravi
nodes.rationale: Original GoEmotions 28-label emotion classification dataset; adapted for literary prose in this work.

nodes.label: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces collective diversity (Doshi & Hauser 2024)
nodes.author: Anil R. Doshi, Oliver P. Hauser
nodes.rationale: Empirical evidence that generative AI reduces diversity in novel content; directly related to narrative flattening findings.

nodes.label: Elias in the lighthouse, again? Diagnosing low diversity in LLM stories (Hamilton & Mimno 2026)
nodes.author: Sil Hamilton, David Mimno
nodes.rationale: Directly addresses low diversity in LLM-generated fiction; contemporary work on same phenomenon.

nodes.label: The curious case of neural text degeneration (Holtzman et al. 2020)
nodes.author: Ari Holtzman, Jan Buys, Li Du, Maxwell Forbes, Yejin Choi
nodes.rationale: Foundational work on neural text degeneration and decoding strategies; relevant to understanding LLM generation patterns.

nodes.label: Understanding the effects of RLHF on LLM generalisation and diversity (Kirk et al. 2024)
nodes.author: Robert Kirk, Ishita Mediratta, Christoforos Nalmpantis, Jelena Luketina, Eric Hambro, Edward Grefenstette, Roberta Raileanu
nodes.rationale: Analyzes RLHF effects on diversity; directly relevant to understanding post-training compression mechanisms.

nodes.label: Diverse preference optimization (Lanchantin et al. 2025)
nodes.author: Jack Lanchantin, Angelica Chen, Shehzaad Dhuliawala, Ping Yu, Jason Weston, Sainbayar Sukhbaatar, Ilia Kulikov
nodes.rationale: Proposes preference optimization method targeting diversity; relevant to understanding alternatives to standard DPO.

nodes.label: Coauthor: Designing a human-AI collaborative writing dataset (Lee et al. 2022)
nodes.author: Mina Lee, Percy Liang, Qian Yang
nodes.rationale: Dataset and analysis of human-AI collaborative writing; provides context for AI writing evaluation.

nodes.label: One fish, two fish, but not the whole sea: Alignment reduces language models' conceptual diversity (Murthy et al. 2025)
nodes.author: Sonia Krishna Murthy, Tomer Ullman, Jennifer Hu
nodes.rationale: Shows alignment reduces conceptual diversity in LLMs; parallel finding to narrative flattening.

nodes.label: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (Ouyang et al. 2022)
nodes.author: Long Ouyang, Jeffrey Wu, Xu Jiang, Diogo Almeida, Carroll Wainwright, Pamela Mishkin, Chong Zhang, Sandhini Agarwal, Katarina Slama, Alex Ray
nodes.rationale: Seminal RLHF paper; foundational to understanding instruction-tuning mechanisms.

nodes.label: Does writing with language models reduce content diversity? (Padmakumar & He 2024)
nodes.author: Vishakh Padmakumar, He He
nodes.rationale: Directly addresses content diversity reduction in LLM writing; core related work.

nodes.label: Narrative theory for computational narrative understanding (Piper et al. 2021)
nodes.author: Andrew Piper, Richard Jean So, David Bamman
nodes.rationale: Theoretical framework for computational narrative analysis; grounds narrative metrics.

nodes.label: Direct preference optimization: Your language model is secretly a reward model (Rafailov et al. 2024)
nodes.author: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma, Eric Mitchell, Stefano Ermon, Christopher D. Manning, Chelsea Finn
nodes.rationale: DPO algorithm paper; one of the post-training stages analyzed in this work.

nodes.label: The emotional arcs of stories are dominated by six basic shapes (Reagan et al. 2016)
nodes.author: Andrew J. Reagan, Lewis Mitchell, Dilan Kiley, Christopher M. Danforth, Peter Sheridan Dodds
nodes.rationale: Foundational work on emotional arcs in narrative; motivates affective analysis approach.

nodes.label: Base models beat aligned models at randomness and creativity (West & Potts 2025)
nodes.author: Peter West, Christopher Potts
nodes.rationale: Shows base models outperform aligned models on creativity metrics; directly supports narrative flattening findings.

nodes.label: Echoes in AI: Quantifying lack of plot diversity in LLM outputs (Xu et al. 2025)
nodes.author: Weijia Xu, Nebojša Jojić, Sudha Rao, Chris Brockett, Bill Dolan
nodes.rationale: Quantifies plot diversity loss in LLM outputs; parallel work on narrative compression.

nodes.label: Verbalized sampling: How to mitigate mode collapse and unlock LLM diversity (Zhang et al. 2025a)
nodes.author: Jiayi Zhang, Simon Yu, Derek Chong, Anthony Sicilia, Michael R Tomz, Christopher D Manning, Weiyan Shi
nodes.rationale: Proposes method to mitigate mode collapse in LLMs; relevant to understanding diversity loss mechanisms.

nodes.label: NoveltyBench: Evaluating language models for humanlike diversity (Zhang et al. 2025b)
nodes.author: Yiming Zhang, Harshita Diddee, Susan Holm, Hanchen Liu, Xinyue Liu, Vinay Samuel, Barry Wang, Daphne Ippolito
nodes.rationale: Benchmark for evaluating LLM diversity; provides evaluation framework for narrative diversity.
